newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - JUNE 2.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - JUNE 2.

text.p: MLADA FRONTA DNES - Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus wants to propose that parliament vote on confidence in the cabinet at its next meeting. His decision was welcomed by President Havel and Klaus's coalition partners.

- According to a survey from Factum, 22.5 percent of Czechs are sure the cabinet can lead the country out of its crisis, while 58 percent believe it cannot. On May 30, 46.3 percent of Czechs recommended that the entire cabinet resign, while on May 18, this amount was only 14.9 percent.

- According to a survey from Factum, 10 percent of citizens trust the new Finance Minister Ivan Pilip, 36 percent trust the new Industry and Trade Minister Karel Kuhnl, and 36.6 percent have confidence in the new Education Minister Jiri Grusa.
- According to the Czech Statistical Bureau, during the first quarter of this year, construction on a total of 3,502 flats was finished, a year-on-year increase of 20.2 percent.

- Alfa-Contakt bought 100 percent of shares of Stasisa Horni Slavkov, the second largest domestic manufacturer of construction and highway machinery, from the National Property Fund for 166 million crowns.
- Ceskoslovenska Plavba Labska signed a contract for the supply of three boats valued at 170 million crowns with Dutch Scheepswerft Peters B.V.
HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - President Vaclav Havel called on fellow citizens yesterday to stay calm and not panic, because the current situation does not call for them to lose hope and fear budget cuts.

- According to the chairman of the Christian Democrats (KDU-CSL) and Cabinet Vice-chairman Josef Lux, Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus kept from the cabinet information from the International Monetary Fund about the economic and currency situation in the Czech Republic.
- Closer analyses of the market show that the crown's drop was not caused by speculation by foreign investors, but by domestic investors.
- The Industry and Trade Ministry will decide on a tender for construction of a new power plant by the end of this year.
- In the next few days, the cabinet should discuss possibilities for covering the debts of Tatra Koprivnice, which amount to 3.5 billion crowns.
- The former majority owner of the daily Prace, Marko Stehlik, sold his majority stake to Ceska Typografie.

- According to the Czech Statistical Bureau, the average gross monthly wage in the first quarter of this year amounted to 9,385 crowns, a decline of 1,700 crowns compared to the end of last year and of 300 crowns compared to the average for the whole of last year.
- According to Michal Krejsa from the European Commission, unprepared state authorities are one of the main obstacles to the Czech Republic's entry into the EU.
PRAVO - Czech Railways signed a contract on Friday with Jindrichohradecke Mistni Drahy a.s. to lease narrow-rail tracks between Jindrichuv Hradec and Nove Bystrice.
- Shareholders of Pragobanka approved an increase in basic capital to 2.86 billion crowns and strengthening its premium fund by one billion crowns to 2.12 billion.
- The European division of Motorola announced it will buy majority shares in Tesla Sezam and Terosil.

LIDOVE NOVINY - According to a survey from Factum, 27.4 percent of Czechs would vote for the opposition Social Democrats (CSSD), while 22.7 percent would vote for the strongest coalition party, the Civic Democratic Party (ODS).

- Justice Minister Vlasta Parkanova announced on Saturday that, together with Interior Minister Jan Ruml, she presented the cabinet with a proposal for a constitutional law to establish 13 supreme territorial self-administered units.
- President Vaclav Havel met with former political prisoners on Saturday and spoke of statesmanship in the fight against Communist despotism.
-- Prague Newsroom, 420-2-2423-0003
